disclaimer: Open tactical data is limited and squads change quickly. These summaries are curated from publicly available analysis and recent match reports, and should be read as indicative rather than definitive.

teams.styleSummary: Compact, disciplined and transition-oriented. Morocco tend to defend in a mid or low block, close central spaces and break quickly through their wide players.
teams.defensiveStyle: Organised mid-to-low block with strong central protection and aggressive duels when pressing triggers appear.
teams.attackingStyle: Fast transitions, combinations in wide areas and late runs from midfield rather than sustained positional play.
weaknesses: Can struggle to create against deep blocks
May become passive when protecting a lead

teams.styleSummary: Flexible and possession-comfortable, with a strong collective identity built under Lionel Scaloni. Recent analyses describe a side that controls midfield, presses in coordinated waves and still creates its decisive moments around Lionel Messi.
teams.defensiveStyle: Well-drilled mid block with energetic counter-pressing after losses; rarely concedes large volumes of chances.
teams.attackingStyle: Patient circulation that accelerates through central combinations; full-backs and midfield runners provide width and depth around the front line.
weaknesses: An ageing core in key positions
A recurring reliance on individual moments to unlock deep defences

teams.styleSummary: Pragmatic and devastating in transition. France tend to concede territory selectively and strike vertically at pace, with the attack heavily oriented towards Kylian Mbappé's side.
teams.defensiveStyle: Medium block with a strong, athletic spine; comfortable defending without the ball for long spells.
teams.attackingStyle: Direct, vertical attacks into the channels; quick release to the left side and runners arriving from midfield.
weaknesses: Can drop too deep and invite pressure
Build-up can look laboured against an organised press

teams.styleSummary: In transition between eras. Under Carlo Ancelotti the side has moved towards a more structured 4-3-3, balancing Brazil's traditional individual expression in wide areas with a more disciplined defensive base.
teams.defensiveStyle: More compact and positionally cautious than earlier cycles; the midfield screens centrally while full-backs pick their moments.
teams.attackingStyle: Wide attackers carrying the ball at pace in one-against-one situations, supported by overlaps and quick central combinations.
strengths: Individual quality in the front line
Pace and unpredictability in wide areas
weaknesses: A recurring pattern is instability from frequent coaching changes
Balance between attacking talents is still being worked out

teams.styleSummary: More direct and front-footed under Thomas Tuchel than in previous cycles. Recent analyses describe a side that wants to win the ball higher and move it forward with fewer touches, built around an experienced attacking core.
teams.defensiveStyle: Higher, more aggressive pressing structure than before, with a back line comfortable defending larger spaces.
teams.attackingStyle: Quicker progression into the final third; Harry Kane dropping to link while runners attack the space beyond him.
weaknesses: One possible weakness is creativity against very deep blocks
A history of conceding momentum in knockout ties

teams.styleSummary: Energetic, well-organised and dangerous in transition. Japan typically alternate between a patient 3-4-2-1 structure and sudden, high-intensity pressing phases that have repeatedly unsettled stronger opponents.
teams.defensiveStyle: Compact 5-4-1 mid block out of possession, with sharp, coordinated pressing triggers in chosen phases.
teams.attackingStyle: Quick vertical breaks through technically strong wide players and wing-backs; intelligent rotations between the lines.
strengths: Squad depth from players in top European leagues
weaknesses: Chance conversion has been a recurring issue
Sustained possession against deep blocks

teams.styleSummary: Athletic and transition-heavy under Mauricio Pochettino, with an emphasis on energy, pressing and quick attacks. As co-hosts, they enter 2026 with a young core that has grown up together.
teams.defensiveStyle: Front-foot pressing in spells, dropping into a compact 4-4-2 block; relies on athleticism to recover space.
teams.attackingStyle: Fast breaks through the wide channels, with Christian Pulisic as the main creative outlet.
weaknesses: Chance creation in settled possession
Limited experience of deep tournament runs

teams.styleSummary: Direct, vertical and ruthlessly efficient. Under Ståle Solbakken, Norway have built a clear identity around fast forward play towards Erling Haaland, with Martin Ødegaard dictating tempo behind him.
teams.defensiveStyle: Disciplined mid block in a 4-4-2 shape; happy to concede possession and protect central areas.
teams.attackingStyle: Quick, direct attacks with early balls into Haaland's running channels; dangerous on set pieces and second balls.
weaknesses: One possible weakness is defending wide areas against quick wingers
Depth beyond the first-choice spine

teams.styleSummary: The tournament's clearest positional-play side. Under Luis de la Fuente, Spain combine their traditional short-passing control with far more direct wing play than earlier eras, built around exceptionally young wide talents.
teams.defensiveStyle: High line and immediate counter-press after losses; opponents rarely get settled possession in Spain's half.
teams.attackingStyle: Patient central build-up that releases quick one-against-one wingers high and wide; midfielders arrive late in the box.
strengths: Elite wide players on both flanks
weaknesses: Can be vulnerable to direct balls in behind the high line
A recurring question is physicality in central defence

teams.styleSummary: Talent-rich and increasingly structured under Roberto Martínez. Recent analyses describe a possession-oriented side with overloads in wide areas, still balancing its system around Cristiano Ronaldo's role in the box.
teams.defensiveStyle: Mid-to-high block with strong individual defenders; pressing intensity varies more than the top pressing sides.
teams.attackingStyle: Patient circulation into wide overloads; creative full-backs and inverted wingers supply a fixed reference striker.
strengths: Depth of creative midfielders and wingers
weaknesses: The balance around an ageing focal point in attack
A tendency to dominate territory without converting it

teams.styleSummary: Structured, physical and pragmatic under Ronald Koeman. The Dutch tend to build calmly from a back three or four, defend with discipline, and rely on a powerful midfield axis rather than classic wing play.
teams.defensiveStyle: Compact, well-organised block with strong aerial defenders; comfortable managing games without dominating them.
teams.attackingStyle: Controlled build-up through central midfield, with full-backs or wing-backs providing the width and late box arrivals from midfield.
weaknesses: Creating high-quality chances against deep blocks
A recurring lack of a prolific central striker

teams.styleSummary: A side renewing itself after its golden generation. Under Rudi Garcia, Belgium are described as more counter-oriented and less possession-dominant than before, organised around a young creative core.
teams.defensiveStyle: Medium block with an emphasis on protecting central areas; less aggressive pressing than the top sides.
teams.attackingStyle: Quick combinations through the half-spaces, with Kevin De Bruyne's successors and Jérémy Doku's carries as the main chance creators.
weaknesses: A defence in generational transition
Recent tournament performances have lagged the talent level

teams.styleSummary: Rebuilt and re-energised under Julian Nagelsmann. Recent analyses describe a high-tempo side that presses aggressively, attacks the half-spaces with quick combinations and has rediscovered a clear identity after a difficult decade of tournaments.
teams.defensiveStyle: High, coordinated pressing with an aggressive line; accepts risk in behind in exchange for territorial control.
teams.attackingStyle: Fast vertical combinations through central zones, with technically elite midfielders arriving between the lines.
weaknesses: Vulnerability to direct play against the high line
A recurring search for a reliable goalscoring striker

teams.styleSummary: Technical, patient and exceptionally tournament-hardened. Croatia under Zlatko Dalić still run games through a high-class midfield, controlling tempo and grinding out tight knockout matches — often via extra time and penalties.
teams.defensiveStyle: Disciplined mid block that prioritises position over pressing; experienced defenders who manage risk well.
teams.attackingStyle: Midfield-led control with measured progression; chances are constructed rather than counter-attacked.
weaknesses: An ageing core, with Luka Modrić's role gradually reduced
Limited pace in wide areas

teams.styleSummary: Expressive and attack-minded under Néstor Lorenzo, with a long unbeaten run in recent years built on technical midfield play and one of the world's most productive creators in James Rodríguez's successor generation — and Luis Díaz at the heart of everything.
teams.defensiveStyle: Medium block with energetic central midfielders; full-backs push high, leaving space that quicker opponents can target.
teams.attackingStyle: Fluid combination play through the left side, with Luis Díaz's dribbling and overlapping full-backs creating overloads.
strengths: Creative quality in the final third
Momentum and confidence from a strong qualifying cycle
weaknesses: Space behind advanced full-backs
A tendency to drop intensity after taking leads

teams.styleSummary: Physical, fast and front-footed. Under Pape Thiaw, Senegal press high from a 4-3-3, counter-press immediately after losses and release their forwards early — with Sadio Mané still the side's reference point, dropping in to link play.
teams.defensiveStyle: Aggressive, coordinated high press backed by athletic, duel-strong defenders and an elite goalkeeper.
teams.attackingStyle: Vertical attacks launched the moment the ball turns over; explosive carries from wide areas and runners breaking beyond the striker.
strengths: Athleticism and duel strength across the pitch
A settled, experienced spine with continental titles
weaknesses: Sustained creation against teams that sit very deep
A reliance on key veterans for composure in big matches

teams.styleSummary: Experienced and pragmatic under Javier Aguirre, hosting the World Cup for a record third time. Recent analyses describe a side that mixes patient possession at home with a more cautious, counter-oriented game against stronger opponents.
teams.defensiveStyle: Organised mid block with experienced central defenders; Aguirre's sides are typically hard to break down rather than aggressive pressers.
teams.attackingStyle: Build-up through wide rotations and full-back overlaps; relies on moments from quick attackers rather than a fixed pattern.
weaknesses: A long-running shortage of elite goalscoring
The round-of-16 ceiling has become its own psychological weight

teams.styleSummary: Intense, brave and unmistakably Marcelo Bielsa's team. Uruguay press man-to-man across the pitch, attack with verticality and numbers, and have traded their traditional pragmatism for one of the most aggressive styles in the tournament.
teams.defensiveStyle: Man-oriented high pressing all over the pitch; physically demanding and deliberately high-risk.
teams.attackingStyle: Direct, fast attacks with runners committed forward in waves; width from touchline wingers and overlapping backs.
weaknesses: Man-marking leaves one-against-one risks at the back
Intensity is hard to sustain across a seven-match tournament

teams.styleSummary: Stable, compact and quietly effective — the tournament's most consistent overachiever. Under Murat Yakin, Switzerland defend in an organised block, control games through technically secure midfielders and rarely beat themselves.
teams.defensiveStyle: Disciplined 4-2-3-1 or back-three block with excellent collective shape; concedes few clear chances.
teams.attackingStyle: Measured build-up through midfield, with set pieces and mid-range strikes as recurring weapons.
weaknesses: A limited ceiling in open attacking play
Reliance on a small group of creators

teams.styleSummary: Resilient, compact and counter-attacking. Under Graham Arnold, Iraq have traded an inconsistent identity for a disciplined low-to-mid block — typically a 4-4-2 that absorbs pressure, keeps possession in the mid-40s and breaks with direct, physical running.
teams.defensiveStyle: Deep, well-organised block with selective pressing; the priority is denying central space and staying in matches.
teams.attackingStyle: Quick, direct transitions towards two strikers, with physical duels and wide running rather than build-up play.
strengths: Composure in decisive matches — qualification went to the wire twice
weaknesses: A large gap in class against top sides
Limited creation when forced to take the initiative
